subs.headline: Bajaj launches the Pulsar N250SS at ₹1.59 lakh with a TFT console and ride modes
subs.text: The N250SS tops the N250 line-up, ₹14,136 above the standard bike. It gets a 5-inch TFT console with Bluetooth and Google Maps mirroring, plus an electronic throttle body that enables ride modes. It comes in four new colours.

subs.headline: Honda Rebel 300 deliveries start around Dhanteras, with BigWing dealers calling first-batch buyers
subs.text: BigWing dealers are telling buyers that deliveries of both the standard and E-Clutch Rebel 300 begin soon. One E-Clutch buyer was offered delivery on 6 November. The Rebel 300 starts at ₹2.22 lakh; the first batch size is not known.

subs.headline: Harley-Davidson X350T spotted undisguised at a dealership, likely a 349cc version of the X440T
subs.text: The X350T carries its name on the tank, with orange paint, a TFT display and upside-down forks. BikeWale expects a 349cc version of the X440T’s 440cc engine, which would fall under the 18 per cent GST rate, against 40 per cent above 350cc. No price or date is confirmed.

headlines.headline: Royal Enfield confirms the Himalayan 750 for EICMA 2026 and shares another teaser
Royal Enfield has five motorcycles due from November, led by the Himalayan 750

trends_summary.headline: Riders search for Harley’s Sprint 440, Hero’s Karizma and Ducati prices ahead of EICMA
trends_summary.text: Searches for “eicma 2026 upcoming motorcycles” broke out as riders look for India-linked bikes such as the Himalayan 750. Harley’s Sprint 440 cruiser and Hero’s Karizma XMR 250 each hold 5000+ searches this week, and “ducati bike price” rose 350% after the Monster Dark unveil.

trending.why: Gaadiwaadi ran a top-five explainer on the upcoming Sprint 440 cruiser, while a Harley X350T was spotted undisguised at a dealership.
Hero plans three to four more premium motorcycles this financial year, and Autocar India expects new Karizma and Xpulse models.
Royal Enfield confirmed the Himalayan 750 for Milan and Rushlane lists the India-linked models expected at EICMA.
Ducati unveiled the Monster V2 Dark, priced at EUR 10,990 in global markets, with an India launch expected in 2027.
